AzureAdCiam._comment: AdditionalAudiences (XD01-390): extra token audiences this kernel accepts besides its own ClientId and api://{ClientId} — CIAM model (b), one app registration per API. GeoAssets.IpBilling.Server and GeoAssets.NeutralOperator.Server validate the caller's token against their own API registration and forward that same token to this kernel's /api/identity/me, /api/identity/policies and /api/identity/organization-grants/me, so list each of their audiences here (their API client id, or App ID URI such as api://<client id>, whichever their tokens carry as aud), e.g. AzureAdCiam__AdditionalAudiences__0=<IpBilling API client id>, AzureAdCiam__AdditionalAudiences__1=<NeutralOperator API client id>. Empty (the default): only the kernel's own audience is accepted, exactly as before; a vertical host whose token the kernel rejects answers 502 kernel.token-rejected. Only the audience set widens — issuer, signature and lifetime are validated as before.

GeoAssets._providersComment: GeoAssets:Providers (XD01-371): the named asset catalogs this host serves, each built at startup by the provider plugin it names ('postgres' is registered by the postgres-spatial module). 'primary' is the default catalog every request reads. A catalog whose plugin no enabled module registers is skipped with a warning.

Tenancy._comment: XD01-471: OrganizationFromMembership = true gives a caller whose token carries no organization claim (Entra CIAM emits none) the organization of their identity record (AppUser.OrganizationId, assigned by an administrator: PUT /api/identity/users/{id}), exactly as if the token carried it, so WMS, WFS, tiles and feature reads show that organization's features. Off by default: an organization caller cannot edit shared (organization-less) features, and its new features are organization-owned. The distributor silos (deploy/distributor-silo) turn it on.

GeoAssets._comment: GeoAssets:Modules (XD01-358/XD01-359): the modules this host enables, in order. 'postgres-spatial' = the PostgreSQL/PostGIS asset store, organization catalogs and WMS; 'neutral-operator' (not listed since the XD01-384 cut-over: GeoAssets.NeutralOperator.Server serves the vertical behind the gateway's /api/v/neutral-operator/**) = shared-use dispatch, pole occupancy, clandestine attachments, ISP tenant portal, the GIS export and the occupancy approval saga — listing it again (e.g. GeoAssets__Modules__1=neutral-operator) is the rollback, together with pointing the gateway's Destinations:NeutralOperator at this host (deploy/neutral-operator/README.md). A blank entry is ignored, so an environment variable such as GeoAssets__Modules__0= disables the module at that position; blank every entry to boot the kernel only. An unknown id fails the startup with the list of known ids — 'ip-billing-bridge' is one since XD01-385 (the município grant bridge is GeoAssets.IpBilling.Server's): remove it from an older configuration.

Outbox._comment: Workflow integration-event transport (XD01-357): the broker the transactional outbox relay publishes the order workflows' integration events to: 'Kafka' (options in a 'WorkflowKafka' section), 'ServiceBus' (options in 'WorkflowServiceBus') or 'None'. With 'None' staged events stay pending in the outbox table until the host runs with a transport, except the approval saga's messages (XD01-383): this host's relay hands the asset mutation batches its modules stage to its own asset-mutation consumer, which applies them to its catalog (GeoAssets:Catalog:InstanceId), and the AppliedV1/RejectedV1 replies back to the modules' saga consumers, in process. With a broker, each saga consumer reads the consumer topic (WorkflowKafkaConsumer:TopicName, or WorkflowServiceBusConsumer:TopicName) in its own group, overridable under WorkflowKafkaConsumer:Consumers:{AssetMutationApply|OccupancyApplySagaApplied|OccupancyApplySagaRejected} (Service Bus: each needs its own Consumers:{key}:SubscriptionName).

Saga._comment: XD01-383: the occupancy approval saga's timeout (while the neutral-operator module is enabled). An approval still awaiting the asset catalog's apply ApplyTimeout after its batch was last staged is flagged (geoassets.saga.apply.timeouts, a structured warning; alert rules in deploy/otel/alerts) and stays pending; POST /api/workflow/service-orders/{id}/occupancy-saga/retry stages it again.
